title: Another World
verdict_short: No. A high-school basketball kid in two soap episodes.
how: Pitt's first speaking TV role: Chris, a teenage basketball player, in the May 14 and 15, 1987 episodes of the NBC soap. The part is a bit role with no dramatic jeopardy; he simply appears and is gone.
notes: Two episodes only.

title: Dallas
verdict_short: No. Charlie Wade's boyfriend gets banned, then un-banned.
how: Across four episodes (December 1987 to February 1988, season 11) Pitt plays Randy, the boyfriend of Charlie Wade. Ray Krebbs forbids Charlie from seeing him for a while, then relents when her behavior improves. Randy simply drifts out of the storyline alive.
notes: Four episodes.

title: Growing Pains
verdict_short: No. Sitcom heartthrob, twice over, never in danger.
how: In "Who's Zoomin' Who?" (November 1987) Pitt is Jeff, the cute transfer student Carol's friends push her toward. In "Feet of Clay" (February 1989) he plays Jonathan Keith, Ben's rock-star idol who turns out to be a jerk backstage. Both are family-sitcom guest spots; nobody dies.
notes: Two different characters across two seasons.
episode: Who's Zoomin' Who? / Feet of Clay

title: 21 Jump Street
verdict_short: No. He's the friend who yells at Penhall, not the kid who dies.
how: In this May 1988 episode, a troubled teen the Jump Street cops are investigating takes his own life, sending Penhall into a spiral. Pitt plays Peter, the boyfriend of a girl in the friend group, who confronts Penhall over his odd behavior. The death is another character; Peter walks away fine.
notes: Some sources list the character as Jeff Deiner; IMDb credits him as Peter.

title: A Stoning in Fulham County
verdict_short: No. He changes his plea to guilty and gets a suspended sentence.
how: Teddy is one of the teens who hurl rocks at an Amish buggy from a pickup, killing a seven-month-old baby. The prosecutor struggles to get the pacifist Amish family to testify. In the courtroom climax Teddy switches his plea to guilty as the Amish family walks in; the epilogue says the boys were fined and given suspended sentences.
notes: NBC TV movie based on a real 1979 Indiana incident.

title: The Dark Side of the Sun
verdict_short: Yes. He takes off the mask, feels the sun, and lets the disease win.
how: Rick has a rare skin disease that makes any light lethal, so he lives in a full leather suit and mask. After a Yugoslav healer fails and the actress he loves rejects his unmasked face, Rick decides to stop hiding: he strips off the protection and feels sunlight on his skin for the first time. The disease then takes its course, and his father accepts the choice he made.
notes: Pitt's first lead. Shot in 1988 in Yugoslavia, unreleased until 1997. The death is implied rather than shown as a drawn-out scene.

title: Trial and Error
verdict_short: No. He carries bags in a sitcom and leaves.
how: Pitt's first paid Hollywood job, shot in November 1987, three days after arriving from Missouri. He plays a hotel bellboy in the second episode of this short-lived CBS sitcom. Zero jeopardy.
notes: Aired March 22, 1988; the series was cancelled after three episodes.

title: Cutting Class
verdict_short: No. Framed for the murders, he survives the drill-in-a-vice finale.
how: Dwight is the bad-boy boyfriend everyone suspects when bodies pile up at school, thanks to a ring with his initials planted at a crime scene. The real killer is asylum-returnee Brian Woods. In the shop-class climax Brian clamps Dwight's head in a vice and goes at him with a drill; Paula brains Brian with a claw hammer and he falls onto a running saw. Dwight and Paula drive off together.
notes: Dark-comedy slasher; Brian (Donovan Leitch) is the one who dies.

title: Freddy's Nightmares
verdict_short: No. Freddy leaves him alive but trapped in adulthood.
how: Newlyweds Rick and Miranda break down in Springwood. Rick's half of the episode is a nightmare gauntlet: he's hit by a hit-and-run driver, robbed by an elderly couple, dreams of piranhas at a motel, and learns he was the hit-and-run driver from the opening. Miranda ends up childlike after a head injury, so Rick is left alive but shackled to responsibility.
notes: Anthology episode "Black Tickets". The nightmares are dream logic, not literal deaths.

title: Happy Together
verdict_short: No. Minor college pal in a rom-com.
how: Pitt's Brian is a small supporting part in this mismatched-roommates college romance starring Patrick Dempsey and Helen Slater. The plot is about the roommates falling in love and finishing their degrees; Brian is peripheral and unharmed.

title: Head of the Class
verdict_short: No. Dim hunk survives a sitcom episode.
how: In the January 1989 episode "Partners", Pitt is Chuck, a handsome but not-so-bright guy that gifted student Maria dumbs herself down to impress. Pure sitcom fluff; nobody is in danger.
notes: Often mislisted as Bobby; IMDb credits the role as Chuck.

title: thirtysomething
verdict_short: No. The babysitter's boyfriend, alive and glowing.
how: Pitt plays Bernard, the boyfriend of the Steadmans' babysitter, in a brief love scene in the season three episode "Love and Sex". Producers said he caused a stir on set. Nothing bad happens to him.

title: Glory Days
verdict_short: No. Cancelled after six episodes, alive.
how: Pitt is Walker Lovejoy, one of four high-school friends drifting apart in this Fox drama. Walker is a college dropout turned cub reporter. The show was cancelled after six episodes with no death for the character.
notes: Fox series, six episodes.

title: The Image
verdict_short: No. Junior newsroom staffer, untouched.
how: In this HBO drama about TV anchor Jason Cromwell (Albert Finney), whose bank-scandal report drives a wrongly accused executive to take his own life, Pitt plays Steve Black, a young reporter on the news team. He's a minor presence and the death is another character's.
notes: HBO TV movie, premiered January 1990.

title: Too Young to Die?
verdict_short: No. The sleazy hustler lives; the girl he corrupted gets the gas chamber.
how: Billy is the drug-dealing hustler who exploits 15-year-old runaway Amanda (Juliette Lewis), pushing her into drugs and strip clubs. After she's dumped by soldier Mike Medwicki, Billy drugs her and goads her into revenge: they kidnap Mike and his girlfriend and Amanda stabs Mike to death with Billy's knife in an oilfield. Both are arrested; the film follows Amanda being tried as an adult and sentenced to death. Billy survives.
notes: Fact-based NBC TV movie.

title: Across the Tracks
verdict_short: No. Runs the big race and keeps breathing.
how: Straight-A track star Joe is chasing a Stanford scholarship when his delinquent brother Billy (Rick Schroder) comes home from juvie and joins a rival school's team. The brothers' rivalry culminates in a head-to-head race with Joe's future on the line. It's a drama about brothers learning a lesson; nobody dies.

title: Johnny Suede
verdict_short: No. Learns life is more than a pair of suede shoes.
how: Pompadoured wannabe rock star Johnny gets magic black suede shoes, chases bohemian Darlette (and dodges her gun-toting boyfriend), pawns his guitar, and loses her. He forms a band with Deke and ends up with the smarter Yvonne, who teaches him there are more important things than shoes. Comic drift, no death.
notes: Pitt's first true starring vehicle in the U.S.

title: Thelma & Louise
verdict_short: No. Steals the cash and walks; the women drive off the cliff.
how: Drifter J.D. charms Thelma into a motel-room night and then robs the women of Louise's $6,700 life savings, which triggers Thelma's turn to armed robbery. He's later picked up and questioned by the police, who use him to help track the women. J.D. is alive and in custody when Thelma and Louise fly the T-bird into the canyon.
notes: Pitt's breakout role.

title: A River Runs Through It
verdict_short: Yes. Beaten to death over gambling debts, off-screen.
how: Charismatic, self-destructive Paul is a brilliant fly fisherman and newspaperman drowning in drink and poker debts. After a last golden day fishing with his father and brother, the police inform Norman that Paul was beaten to death; his body was found in an alley with the bones of his casting hand broken. The circumstances are left deliberately mysterious.
notes: Death reported, never shown. Based on Norman Maclean's real brother.

title: Contact
verdict_short: No. Buries a dead Iraqi soldier and parts ways with the other.
how: Lost in the Iraqi desert during the Gulf War, American soldier Cox picks his way through a minefield and comes face-to-face with Iraqi soldier Mohannan (Elias Koteas). He can't pull the trigger after seeing Mohannan look at a family photo. A poison-gas warning forces them to cooperate; the film ends with the two burying a dead Iraqi and going their separate ways.
notes: 30-minute short, Oscar-nominated for Best Live Action Short.

title: Cool World
verdict_short: Yes. Holli shoves him off a Vegas hotel roof. Then he's reborn as a cartoon.
how: Detective Frank Harris, a WWII vet stuck in the animated Cool World since 1945, tries to stop Holli Would from escaping into the real world. In the climax atop the Union Plaza Hotel, Holli pushes him off the building to his death. But a 'noid' killed by a 'doodle' in the real world is reborn as a doodle, so Frank returns to Cool World as a cartoon and can finally be with Lonette.
notes: Dies as a human, resurrected as an animated character. Counts as a death with a happy loophole.

title: Tales from the Crypt
verdict_short: Yes. Loses the drag race to the Iceman and goes up in a fireball.
how: Cocky psycho drag racer Billy rolls into town to goad Sheriff Joe Garrett, secretly the legendary racer 'Iceman', into one last race. When Joe refuses, Billy seduces and then kidnaps his daughter Carey to force him behind the wheel. In the midnight race Billy slams into a digger parked in the road and dies in a fireball while Joe wins.
notes: Season 4 episode "King of the Road", directed by Tom Holland. Also released as a segment of the compilation TV film Two-Fisted Tales (1992).

title: Kalifornia
verdict_short: Yes. Shot dead by the writer he terrorized.
how: Kentucky parolee Early Grayce joins writer Brian and photographer Carrie on a cross-country serial-killer road trip and turns out to be a killer himself, murdering strangers and finally shooting his own girlfriend Adele. At an abandoned nuclear test site he kidnaps Carrie. Carrie clubs him with a mannequin limb, and when he keeps coming Brian shoots him dead.

title: True Romance
verdict_short: No. Never leaves the couch or the honey-bear bong.
how: Floyd is Dick Ritchie's perma-stoned roommate who spends the whole movie on the sofa. He cheerfully gives the Mafia hitmen the location of the drug deal and later does the same for the cops, but nobody bothers to hurt him. The Beverly Ambassador shootout happens without him.
notes: Scene-stealing cameo.

title: Interview with the Vampire
verdict_short: No. He's been undead since 1791 and still is.
how: Louis, turned by Lestat in 1791, is the immortal narrator telling his story to a journalist in 1990s San Francisco. He survives Lestat's attempted murders, the Théâtre des Vampires burning, and centuries of misery. The film ends with a revived Lestat attacking the interviewer in his car, but Louis himself is very much still around.
notes: Technically 'dead' as a vampire, but the character never perishes. Claudia, not Louis, is destroyed by sunlight.

title: Legends of the Fall
verdict_short: Yes. Killed fighting a grizzly bear as an old man in 1963.
how: After a life of war, grief, bootlegging and revenge, Tristan outlives nearly everyone he loves. The epilogue, narrated by One Stab, jumps to 1963: an aged Tristan investigating an animal carcass in the North Country is confronted by a grizzly. He draws his knife and fights it, and dies in the struggle, a 'good death' that bookends the bear that clawed him at age twelve.
notes: Shown briefly on screen and narrated. Samuel, Isabel Two and Susannah all die before him.

title: The Favor
verdict_short: No. Ends up planning a wedding.
how: Elliott is Emily's young artist boyfriend in this rom-com about Kathy asking her best friend to sleep with her old flame. Emily gets pregnant, Kathy meddles about the paternity, but once it's clear the baby is Elliott's he steps up. The film ends with Kathy helping Emily plan her wedding to Elliott.
notes: Shot in 1991, shelved until 1994.

title: 12 Monkeys
verdict_short: No. The twitchy red herring survives; the plague isn't even his.
how: Jeffrey Goines is the mental-patient son of a virologist who founds the Army of the Twelve Monkeys. Cole assumes he's behind the apocalyptic virus, but Jeffrey's big crime turns out to be releasing zoo animals. Cole is the one shot dead at the airport; Jeffrey is last seen alive and unhinged.
notes: Oscar-nominated supporting turn.

title: Seven
verdict_short: No. He lives, but what's in the box destroys him anyway.
how: Rookie detective Mills hunts the seven-deadly-sins killer John Doe alongside Somerset. In the desert finale a delivery box arrives containing the head of Mills' pregnant wife Tracy; Doe confesses he is 'envy' and that Mills must become 'wrath'. Mills shoots Doe dead, completing the killer's design, and is led away alive but broken.
notes: Tracy (Gwyneth Paltrow) dies off-screen; Mills survives.

title: Sleepers
verdict_short: No. Throws the case, quits, and becomes a carpenter in England.
how: Michael, one of four Hell's Kitchen boys abused at a juvenile home, grows up to be an assistant DA who deliberately sabotages his own prosecution of his friends for killing guard Nokes, exposing the other abusers. The epilogue says Michael quits the DA's office, moves to the English countryside and becomes a carpenter. His friends John and Tommy die young; Michael doesn't.

title: Seven Years in Tibet
verdict_short: No. Goes home to Austria and takes his son climbing.
how: Austrian mountaineer Harrer is interned by the British in India, escapes to Tibet, and becomes tutor and friend to the young Dalai Lama. When China invades in 1950 he leaves Tibet and returns to Austria, where he reconciles with the son who once rejected him. The film closes with the two climbing together.
notes: The real Harrer lived until 2006.

title: The Devil's Own
verdict_short: Yes. Shot in a final boat standoff with the cop who took him in.
how: IRA gunman Frankie McGuire hides as 'Rory Devaney' with NYPD sergeant Tom O'Meara's family while buying Stinger missiles. Once exposed, he boards a boat to sail the weapons home. Tom follows; in the shootout Tom is wounded and disarmed, and Frankie is about to finish him when he realizes he too has been shot. He dies in Tom's arms as Tom steers the boat back to shore.

title: Meet Joe Black
character: Joe Black / the young man in the coffee shop
verdict_short: Yes and no. The coffee-shop guy is flattened by two cars; Death borrows his body, then gives it back alive.
how: Early on, the charming young man Susan meets in a coffee shop steps into the street and is fatally struck by multiple cars in one of cinema's most replayed deaths. Death then wears his body as 'Joe Black' to shadow Bill Parrish. At the end Joe walks Bill over the bridge into the afterlife, and the original young man returns, alive and unaware of where he's been, to rekindle things with Susan.
notes: The body dies at the start and is restored at the end; Death itself obviously can't die. Pitt plays both.

title: Saturday Night Live
verdict_short: No. Plays David Spade's shrink in the cold open.
how: In the November 7, 1998 cold open, David Spade visits his therapist, played by Pitt, to complain about the burdens of fame. It's a one-sketch cameo with no peril.
notes: Season 24. Sketch appearance, not a hosting gig.

title: Being John Malkovich
verdict_short: No. On screen for about half a second, mid-frown.
how: In the mock documentary about Malkovich's puppeteering career, Pitt appears as himself for a split second, looking miffed and about to speak before the cut. No fate, no lines.
notes: Uncredited cameo.

title: Fight Club
verdict_short: Sort of. The Narrator shoots himself through the cheek and Tyler blinks out of existence. But Tyler was never real.
how: Tyler Durden is revealed to be the Narrator's dissociated alter ego. With Project Mayhem's bombs about to level the credit-card towers, the Narrator realizes the gun in Tyler's hand is really in his own and fires it through his cheek. Tyler, gushing blood from the back of his head, collapses and vanishes. The Narrator survives, and he and Marla watch the buildings fall.
notes: Tyler is a hallucination; his 'death' is the Narrator's psyche reasserting control. The body Pitt plays never physically existed.

title: Snatch
verdict_short: No. Fakes taking a dive, wins the fight, and his camp settles up with Brick Top.
how: Bare-knuckle champion Mickey is ordered by gangster Brick Top to throw a fight; when Mickey refuses, Brick Top has his mother burned alive in her caravan. Mickey pretends to comply, then knocks his opponent out in the fourth round while his people ambush and kill Brick Top and his men outside. The travellers vanish before dawn.
notes: Mickey's mum dies; Mickey doesn't.

title: Friends
verdict_short: No. Storms out of Thanksgiving still hating Rachel Green.
how: Ross's formerly-fat high-school friend Will comes to Monica's Thanksgiving and reveals he and Ross co-founded the 'I Hate Rachel Green Club' and spread a nasty rumor about her. The episode ends with Will, Ross and Rachel bickering and everyone alive.
notes: Pitt and Jennifer Aniston were married at the time. Emmy-nominated guest turn.

title: Ocean's Eleven
verdict_short: No. Eats his way through a $160M heist and drives off with Danny.
how: Rusty is Danny Ocean's right hand in the Bellagio vault job. The crew pulls off the heist, Benedict is fooled, and Rusty is last seen picking Danny up outside prison with Tess in tow. Perpetually snacking, never in danger.

title: Spy Game
verdict_short: No. Muir buys him out of a Chinese prison with Operation Dinner Out.
how: Bishop is caught by the Chinese trying to spring his lover Elizabeth Hadley from prison and is scheduled for execution within 24 hours. Retiring mentor Nathan Muir spends his last day at Langley, and his own savings, faking authorization for a Navy SEAL rescue. Bishop and Hadley are lifted out by helicopter, and Bishop realizes Muir saved him when the pilot names the op.

title: The Mexican
verdict_short: No. Delivers the cursed pistol, keeps the girl, drives into the sunset.
how: Bungling errand boy Jerry is sent to Mexico to retrieve the legendary 'Mexican' pistol while his girlfriend Sam is held by hitman Leroy. Bodies drop around him, including Leroy and mob boss Margolese's rival, but Jerry survives every mishap, returns the gun to Margolese, and ends the film on the road with Sam.

title: Confessions of a Dangerous Mind
verdict_short: No. He just loses on The Dating Game.
how: In George Clooney's directorial debut, Pitt and Matt Damon sit on stools in period wigs and loud 1970s outfits as two contestants on Chuck Barris's The Dating Game. The bachelorette ignores them entirely, and neither gets a line; the joke restages the real-life fact that Burt Reynolds and Tom Selleck went unpicked on the show. Pitt's screen time is a few seconds, and he simply isn't chosen.
notes: Blink-and-miss-it cameo done as a favor to Clooney. No peril of any kind.

title: Full Frontal
verdict_short: No. Just Brad Pitt being Brad Pitt on a film set.
how: Pitt appears as himself in Soderbergh's meta Hollywood comedy, showing up on the set of the movie-within-the-movie where actor Nicholas (Blair Underwood) is pulled away to shoot a scene alongside him. His only stake in the story is being reassured that his movie is 'the real movie.' He is never in any peril and simply exits the story as the day-in-the-life plot moves on.
notes: Celebrity cameo as himself; not a character with a fate.

title: Jackass
verdict_short: No. Kidnapped at Pink's Hot Dogs, but it's a prank.
how: Pitt turned up in two Season 3 episodes of MTV's Jackass in 2002. In 'Night Monkey 2' he dons a gorilla suit with Johnny Knoxville, Bam Margera, Chris Pontius and Steve-O and rampages through the streets of Los Angeles. In 'The Abduction' he stands in line at Pink's Hot Dogs in Hollywood when masked men grab him, drag him thrashing into a van and drive off while horrified bystanders try to intervene. It's all staged; he walks away unharmed.
notes: Reality/prank TV, no fictional character. Pitt does not appear in Jackass Number Two (2006) despite frequent misattribution.

title: King of the Hill
verdict_short: No. Dumped at the altar for being a sleaze.
how: Boomhauer's womanizing brother Patch rolls into Arlen in a Saab convertible to marry Katherine (Laura Dern), Boomhauer's old flame. Boomhauer quits as best man and Hank steps in, assuming Boomhauer is sabotaging the wedding, until it becomes clear Patch is the one sneaking around. When Patch blurts out the truth, Katherine hands back the ring and calls off the engagement. Patch is left humiliated but alive.
notes: Season 8 premiere, aired November 2, 2003. Pitt, a fan of the show, pitched the idea of voicing Boomhauer's brother; the character speaks in the same Boomhauer mumble.

title: Sinbad: Legend of the Seven Seas
verdict_short: No. The executioner's sword shatters mid-swing.
how: Framed by the goddess Eris for stealing the Book of Peace, Sinbad is sentenced to death, but Prince Proteus takes his place as hostage while Sinbad sails to Tartarus to recover it. Eris offers Sinbad a bargain: if he answers truthfully whether he'll return to face execution, she'll surrender the Book. He returns to Syracuse and kneels for the blade, but because he answered honestly, an enraged Eris must honor the deal, shattering the executioner's sword and delivering the Book. Sinbad is pardoned and sails off with Marina, who stows away on his ship.
notes: Comes within a sword-swing of a beheading in the climax but is saved by divine contract. Animated voice role.

title: Ocean's Twelve
verdict_short: No. Out-cons the Night Fox and gets the girl.
how: Rusty is Danny Ocean's right hand as the crew scrambles across Europe to repay Terry Benedict, competing with the Night Fox to steal the Fabergé Coronation Egg. His ex, Europol detective Isabel Lahiri, lifts his phone and arrests most of the gang, but it turns out the real egg was swiped by Linus's parents and mentor Gaspar LeMarc days earlier. Rusty ends the film taking Isabel to a safe house where she meets her father, LeMarc, and the crew walks free.
notes: Nobody in the crew is ever in mortal danger; the stakes are financial and legal.

title: Troy
verdict_short: Yes. Paris's arrow finds the famous heel.
how: During the sack of Troy, Achilles ignores the slaughter and searches the burning city for Briseis. He finds her just as Paris, seeking vengeance for Hector, puts an arrow through his heel and then several more into his chest. Achilles pulls the body-shots out so that only the heel wound is seen, watches Briseis flee with Paris, and dies on the temple steps. Odysseus cremates him in the closing funeral scene and narrates his legend.
notes: Follows the myth's heel wound, though the film has Paris finish him with multiple arrows to the torso; Achilles yanks those out so the legend of the single heel shot can stand.

title: Mr. & Mrs. Smith
verdict_short: No. Survives his wife and a store full of assassins.
how: Rival contract killers John and Jane Smith discover they've been married to the enemy and set about killing each other, leveling their suburban house in a shootout. With guns drawn they realize they can't pull the trigger, reconcile, and learn their agencies have ordered both of them dead. They make a last stand in a home-improvement store, mowing down waves of hitmen, and the film ends with the couple back in marriage counseling, beaming about how well things are going.
notes: John takes plenty of punishment from Jane but nothing fatal.

title: Babel
verdict_short: No. His wife takes the bullet, and she lives too.
how: Richard and Susan are American tourists in Morocco, their marriage strained by the recent crib death of their infant son, when a stray rifle shot fired by two goat-herder boys hits Susan through the tour-bus window. Richard drags her to a remote village, where a local vet stitches the wound and the other tourists abandon them. After an agonizing wait, a helicopter finally airlifts them to a hospital in Casablanca, where Susan is expected to recover. Richard is never physically harmed.
notes: The wounded character is Cate Blanchett's Susan, not Pitt's Richard; she survives.

title: Ocean's Thirteen
verdict_short: No. Walks off grinning after a rigged $11 million slot win.
how: Rusty helps Danny orchestrate revenge on casino mogul Willy Bank, who cheated their friend Reuben into a heart attack. The crew rigs every game on The Bank's opening night, fakes an earthquake with a tunnel-boring drill, and empties the casino. In the final scene at the airport, Rusty gives his last coin to the real Five Diamond reviewer, who wins $11 million on a rigged slot machine as Rusty strolls away smiling.
notes: Third and final Rusty appearance; no physical danger at any point.

title: The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford
verdict_short: Yes. Shot in the back of the head by Robert Ford.
how: On the morning of April 3, 1882, in his St. Joseph, Missouri home, Jesse reads a newspaper report of Dick Liddil's surrender and realizes the Fords have betrayed him. Seemingly resigned, he removes his gun belt, climbs onto a chair and turns his back to dust a framed picture on the wall. Robert Ford draws the nickel-plated revolver Jesse had gifted him days earlier and shoots him in the back of the head. Jesse crumples to the floor, dead, and the Fords flee to claim the reward.
notes: The film strongly implies Jesse knows what's coming and allows it. The death occurs roughly two hours in, followed by a long epilogue tracing Ford's own downfall and murder.

title: Burn After Reading
verdict_short: Yes. Shot in the face in a closet by Harry Pfarrer.
how: Dim, exuberant gym trainer Chad breaks into Osborne Cox's house to dig up more 'intelligence' and hides in a bedroom closet when Harry Pfarrer (George Clooney), a jumpy U.S. Marshal sleeping with Cox's wife, comes home. Harry opens the closet door, Chad grins nervously, and Harry reflexively shoots him in the head. Finding no ID and the tags cut from Chad's suit, Harry concludes he's killed a government spy and dumps the body. The CIA later finds the corpse and quietly buries the whole affair.
notes: Abrupt, played for shock comedy; Chad's death comes roughly two-thirds through and derails every character's scheme.

title: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
verdict_short: Yes. Dies of old age as a newborn in Daisy's arms.
how: Born in 1918 with the body of an old man and aging backward, Benjamin spends his last years regressing into childhood. In 1990 Daisy finds him as a pre-teen with dementia and takes him into the nursing home where he was raised; he shrinks into a toddler, then an infant, his mind fading. In spring 2003, chronologically 85 but physically a newborn, he looks up at Daisy, seems to recognize her, closes his eyes and dies in her arms. Daisy recounts all this from her own deathbed in 2005 as Hurricane Katrina approaches.
notes: The whole film is narrated from Benjamin's diary by a dying Daisy, so his death is both shown and framed as memory.

title: Inglourious Basterds
verdict_short: No. Carves his masterpiece into Landa's forehead.
how: Aldo 'the Apache' Raine leads the Basterds' Nazi-scalping campaign through occupied France and gets captured by Col. Hans Landa at the Paris premiere after a bungled Italian cover. Landa cuts a deal with the Allies to let Operation Kino proceed, and Hitler, Goebbels and the Nazi high command burn and are shot to pieces inside the cinema. Driving Raine and Utivich to American lines, Landa surrenders; Raine shoots Landa's radio operator and, deciding a deal shouldn't let Landa take off his uniform, carves a swastika into his forehead with his knife.
notes: Raine is captured and beaten but never seriously hurt. Donowitz and Ulmer die in the cinema blast; Raine and Utivich are the survivors.

title: Megamind
verdict_short: No. Fakes his death to become Music Man.
how: Early on, Megamind lures Metro Man to the old observatory and blasts him with a sun-powered death ray, apparently vaporizing him; the hero had claimed the copper-lined dome weakened his powers, and only a charred cape and skeleton are left. Metro City mourns and Megamind takes over, then grows bored without a nemesis. Midway through, Megamind and Roxanne discover Metro Man alive in his secret hideout, where he confesses he faked the copper weakness and his own death because he was burned out on heroing and wants to play guitar. He returns in disguise at the end to cheer Megamind's turn as the city's hero.
notes: Fake death: staged by death ray in the first act, revealed as a hoax at the midpoint. Metro Man is alive and well at the end.

title: Happy Feet Two
verdict_short: No. A krill who refuses to be eaten and becomes a legend.
how: Will, an existentially restless krill, drags his friend Bill (Matt Damon) away from the swarm to climb the food chain, only to learn he's at the very bottom of it. After a series of near-misses with whales and predators, a humbled Will reunites with Bill and the swarm, where they're hailed as legends for their journey. In the finale Will and the krill join the penguins, elephant seals and Sven in the mass effort to shatter the iceberg trapping the emperor penguins.
notes: Comic side plot; despite being prey, neither krill is eaten. Animated voice role.

title: Moneyball
verdict_short: No. Turns down $12.5 million and stays in Oakland.
how: Oakland A's general manager Billy Beane rebuilds a gutted roster on sabermetrics with Yale economist Peter Brand, endures a brutal start, and rides a record 20-game winning streak capped by Scott Hatteberg's walk-off homer. The A's win the AL West but lose the divisional series to Minnesota. The Red Sox offer Beane the richest GM contract in sports history; he declines it to stay near his daughter, listening to her song in his car as the film closes.
notes: Biographical; the real Billy Beane is alive. No physical peril in the film beyond thrown chairs.

title: The Tree of Life
verdict_short: No. It's his son who dies; he outlives the boy.
how: The film opens with Mr. and Mrs. O'Brien receiving the telegram that their 19-year-old son R.L. has died in the 1960s, and the rest unfolds as older son Jack's memories of a 1950s Texas childhood under his stern, frustrated father. Mr. O'Brien, an engineer and thwarted musician, loses a patent suit and his plant closes, and in a moment of humility asks Jack's forgiveness before the family moves away. He is last seen alive, and in the film's beach-of-eternity coda the whole family, R.L. included, is reunited.
notes: The film's central death is R.L.'s, delivered by telegram in the opening minutes. The afterlife/beach sequence is metaphysical, not a literal death of Mr. O'Brien.

title: Killing Them Softly
verdict_short: No. America's not a country, it's a business. Now pay him.
how: Mob enforcer Jackie Cogan is brought in to clean up after a protected card game is robbed, and he does: he has Markie Trattman gunned down in his car, blasts Squirrel with a shotgun at a meet, and shoots Frankie in the head without warning in a parking garage. Nobody ever gets a shot at Jackie himself. On election night 2008 he meets the mob's lawyer Driver in a bar, is offered a discounted fee, and delivers the closing monologue before demanding his full money.
notes: Jackie is the film's only unscathed principal; Mickey (Gandolfini) is arrested and everyone else is killed.

title: 12 Years a Slave
verdict_short: No. The Canadian carpenter who mails the letter that frees Solomon.
how: Late in the film, Canadian itinerant laborer Samuel Bass arrives at Edwin Epps's plantation to build a gazebo alongside Solomon Northup and openly argues with Epps that slavery is an abomination. After Solomon confides that he is a kidnapped free man, Bass risks his life to write to Solomon's friends in Saratoga, New York. The letter brings the sheriff and shopkeeper Mr. Parker to the plantation, and Solomon is freed after twelve years. Bass simply finishes his work and departs unharmed.
notes: Small but pivotal role near the end of the film; Pitt also produced through Plan B.

title: The Counselor
verdict_short: Yes. Decapitated on a London street by the bolito.
how: Middleman Westray, who earlier warned the Counselor about the cartel's 'bolito', a motorized wire loop that tightens until it cuts through the neck, flees to London with his money when the drug deal goes bad. Malkina hires a woman to seduce him and steal his bank codes, then has her men snatch his laptop and drop the bolito over his head on a crowded sidewalk. The device whirs tighter as Westray claws at it and collapses in a spreading pool of blood, and the wire finally severs his head. Malkina drains his accounts and escapes.
notes: One of the most infamous death scenes of the 2010s; the device is foreshadowed in Westray's own earlier monologue.

title: World War Z
verdict_short: No. Injects himself with a deadly pathogen and walks right past the zombies.
how: Ex-UN investigator Gerry Lane survives the Philadelphia outbreak, a rooftop extraction in Newark, the fall of Jerusalem, and a plane crash outside Cardiff that leaves him impaled by shrapnel. At the WHO lab he theorizes that the undead ignore the terminally ill, so with a zombie blocking the vault door he injects himself with a lethal but curable pathogen, walks untouched through the infected wing, and is cured. He reaches his family at a Nova Scotia safe zone as a 'camouflage' vaccine turns the tide.
notes: Comes close several times. The famously reshot third act replaced a bleaker Moscow ending in which Gerry also survived.

title: Fury
verdict_short: Yes. Goes down with his tank, shredded by grenades in a last stand.
how: In April 1945 Wardaddy's immobilized Sherman, 'Fury', makes a suicidal last stand at a crossroads against a Waffen-SS battalion. As ammo runs out he is hit by a German sniper, then, bleeding out inside the turret, orders Norman to escape through the floor hatch. SS troops drop stick grenades into the tank and the blasts kill him. The next morning Norman climbs back in and covers his corpse with his jacket before US reinforcements find him.
notes: He is the only member of the crew besides Norman who survives long enough to make the final choice; the rest of the crew die one by one in the same battle.

title: By the Sea
verdict_short: No. Finishes his novel and drives off with his wife.
how: Roland, a blocked American writer, spends a 1970s French seaside holiday drinking while his wife Vanessa (Angelina Jolie) grieves. The pair spy on newlyweds through a hole in the wall, Vanessa tries to seduce the young husband, and Roland punches him. The marriage's wound turns out to be Vanessa's miscarriages and infertility. They reconcile, Roland finishes his book about her, and they leave the hotel together, alive and slightly more hopeful.
notes: Written and directed by his then-wife Angelina Jolie; their last film together.

title: The Audition
verdict_short: No. He just steals the part from De Niro and DiCaprio.
how: A 16-minute promotional short for a Macau casino. Robert De Niro and Leonardo DiCaprio each pitch Martin Scorsese on why they should star in his next picture, only for Scorsese to reveal he has already cast Brad Pitt, who strolls in playing a smug version of himself. Nobody dies; the joke is the two stunned actors congratulating each other.
notes: Short film; reportedly the most expensive short ever made.

title: The Big Short
verdict_short: No. Cashes out and goes back to growing seeds in retirement.
how: Ben Rickert, a paranoid retired trader, helps two young investors (Charlie and Jamie) get the swaps that let them bet against the housing market. When the crash finally hits he sells their positions from a pub in England, scolding them for celebrating an economy's collapse. The epilogue notes he simply returned to his quiet retirement, alive and grumpy.
notes: Character is based on real trader Ben Hockett. Pitt also produced the film.

title: Allied
verdict_short: No. He lives; his wife shoots herself on the runway.
how: Canadian intelligence officer Max Vatan marries French Resistance fighter Marianne after their Casablanca assassination mission, then learns she may be a German spy. Ordered to execute her if the 'blue dye' test proves it, Max instead kills her handlers and tries to fly her out. As military police close in on the airfield, Marianne tells Max she loves him, asks him to care for their daughter, and shoots herself. Max survives and raises Anna on a ranch in Medicine Hat, Alberta.

title: The Jim Jefferies Show
verdict_short: No. He just forecasts the end of the world.
how: Pitt turned up in the Comedy Central show's June 2017 premiere as a deadpan, tan-suited weatherman standing in front of a glowing red map after the U.S. pulled out of the Paris climate accord ('things are going to be getting warmer in this area here'). He returned several times across 2017 and 2018 as the show's unofficial, increasingly depressed weatherman. Nobody dies, but the planet is not doing great.
notes: Seven episodes, 2017 to 2018. Pitt reportedly asked to be on the show and was paid SAG scale.

title: War Machine
verdict_short: No. Fired by the President after a Rolling Stone exposé.
how: McMahon, a swaggering four-star general (a thinly veiled Stanley McChrystal), arrives in Afghanistan in 2009 to 'win' the war and pushes for a 40,000-troop surge. He leaks his assessment, mouths off about the President, and lets a Rolling Stone reporter embed with his staff. The resulting article exposes his contempt for civilian leadership and he is summoned to Washington and relieved of command, quietly lining up a consultant gig on the way out. A new general is appointed to keep the war going.
notes: Netflix release. Satire based on Michael Hastings' book The Operators.

title: Deadpool 2
verdict_short: Yes. Electrocuted on power lines, visible for about one second.
how: The invisible mutant Vanisher joins Deadpool's new X-Force team for a parachute drop onto a prison convoy. High winds scatter the team and kill them one by one; Vanisher is blown into high-voltage power lines and electrocuted, his face flickering into view for a split second to reveal it was Brad Pitt all along. Only Deadpool and Domino survive the jump.
notes: Uncredited surprise cameo; Pitt shot it in about two hours for scale. The same footage appears in the PG-13 recut Once Upon a Deadpool (2018). Deadpool's time-travel fix at the end saves Peter but not Vanisher.

title: Ad Astra
verdict_short: No. Nukes his dad's space station and rides the shockwave home to Earth.
how: Roy travels to Neptune to stop the antimatter surges from his father's lost Lima Project station. He finds his father Clifford (Tommy Lee Jones) alive and unrepentant after killing his mutinous crew, plants a nuclear charge, and tries to bring him home. Clifford instead pushes off into space and asks to be let go; Roy releases the tether and watches him drift away. Roy uses the blast to slingshot back to Earth, where he lands safely and reconnects with his estranged wife.
notes: His father dies; Roy survives everything, including a Moon pirate chase and a rabid space baboon.

title: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
verdict_short: No. Stabbed in the hip, but he beats the Manson Family to death and rides off in an ambulance.
how: On August 8, 1969, Cliff, tripping on an acid-dipped cigarette, is walking Brandy the pit bull when three Manson Family members break into Rick Dalton's house instead of Sharon Tate's. Cliff sics Brandy on Tex, stomps him to death, and after Katie stabs him in the hip he smashes her face in with a can of dog food and anything else within reach; Rick torches the third intruder with a flamethrower. Cliff is loaded into an ambulance alive, joking with Rick, while Rick gets invited up to Sharon Tate's house for a drink.
notes: Won Pitt the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor.

title: Saturday Night Live
verdict_short: No. Takes off the wig and thanks the real Fauci.
how: In the April 25, 2020 remote cold open, Pitt plays Dr. Fauci calmly 'translating' clips of the President's coronavirus statements, facepalming at the disinfectant and 'hit the body with light' ideas. At the end he removes the gray wig and glasses and, as himself, thanks Fauci and frontline workers. Nobody dies.
notes: Earned Pitt an Emmy nomination for Outstanding Guest Actor in a Comedy Series.

title: Babylon
verdict_short: Yes. Shoots himself in a hotel room once the talkies leave him behind.
how: Silent-era megastar Jack Conrad can't survive the transition to sound; audiences laugh at his voice and he's shoved into ensemble parts. In 1932, after his friend George Munn takes his own life, Jack confronts gossip columnist Elinor St. John, who tells him his star has faded but the films will make him immortal. He runs into Fay at a hotel party, learns she's leaving for Europe, returns to his room, and shoots himself; the gunshot is heard from the hallway.
notes: Death comes roughly two hours into the three-hour film, before the Manny and Nellie finale.

title: Bullet Train
verdict_short: No. Everyone else dies; his bad luck keeps him alive.
how: Anxious assassin Ladybug boards a Tokyo-to-Kyoto bullet train to grab a briefcase and instead gets tangled with Lemon, Tangerine, the Prince, the Hornet, and eventually the White Death. In the derailed wreckage the White Death shoots Ladybug with Ladybug's own gun, which the Prince had rigged to backfire, blowing off the villain's head. Ladybug limps out of the ruins into Maria's (Sandra Bullock) car, alive and complaining.
notes: Nearly everyone else on the train dies.

title: The Lost City
verdict_short: No. But he's shot in the head and looks very dead until the mid-credits scene.
how: Jack Trainer, a glorious-haired ex-Navy SEAL, storms Fairfax's jungle compound and rescues Loretta (Sandra Bullock) in a one-man action sequence. During the escape he is shot in the head by a mercenary in front of a horrified Alan (Channing Tatum), and the movie treats him as dead for the rest of the runtime. In a mid-credits scene Loretta and Alan spot him alive at a meditation class; he shrugs that only 10% of his brain was in use anyway.
notes: Extended cameo of about 15 minutes. Apparent death around the end of act one; revealed alive mid-credits.

title: Dave
verdict_short: No. Takes a crossbow bolt to the chest but gives a thumbs-up to the paramedics.
how: After popping into Lil Dicky's 'Mr. McAdams' music video, Pitt shows up at Dave's house wanting a music mentor and ends up recording in his studio, only for obsessed fan Bella to take them (and GaTa) hostage at gunpoint. At the peak of the standoff Bella shoots Brad in the chest with a tour-branded arrow from Dave's prop crossbow. Bleeding out, he dispenses one last piece of wisdom ('Until you love yourself, you can never love another'); as paramedics rush in his hand rises in a thumbs-up, signalling he'll live.
notes: Aired May 31, 2023 on FXX. Outcome kept slightly ambiguous, but the creators and the thumbs-up confirm he survives.

title: IF
verdict_short: No. He's an invisible imaginary friend; you never see or hear him.
how: Keith is an invisible, silent imaginary friend that characters keep tripping over throughout John Krasinski's film. Pitt has no lines and no on-screen presence; his credit only appears at the end as a wink at his invisible Vanisher cameo in Deadpool 2 (also with Ryan Reynolds). No death, no body, no character arc.
notes: Credited voice cameo with zero audible dialogue.

title: Wolfs
verdict_short: No. Cuts to black as the diner shootout starts.
how: Two rival lone-wolf fixers (Pitt and George Clooney) are hired to clean up the same hotel-room 'corpse', which turns out to be a very alive kid full of drugs. After a night dodging Albanian mobsters and returning the stolen product, both are ordered to kill the Kid but choose not to. In the final scene hitmen surround them at a Brighton Beach diner; they agree to finally tell each other their names if they survive, start shooting, and the film cuts to black.
notes: Open-ended, but no death shown. Apple TV+ release; a planned sequel was cancelled.

title: F1
verdict_short: No. Wins Abu Dhabi and drives off to the next race.
how: Aging journeyman Sonny Hayes returns to Formula One with the failing APXGP team thirty years after a near-fatal 1993 crash. He walks away from more crashes (Silverstone, a fiery Las Vegas pileup that briefly gets him fired, a minor Abu Dhabi shunt) while hiding that his old injuries make him medically unfit to race. In the Abu Dhabi finale he holds off Lewis Hamilton, takes his first F1 win, saves the team, and is last seen heading off to race in Baja.
notes: Sonny's teammate Joshua Pearce also survives a serious crash.

title: Heart of the Beast
verdict_short: Yes. His failing heart gives out in the Alaskan wilderness; only the dog makes it to the road.
how: Retired Special Forces operator James Belmont suffers a heart attack while piloting a seaplane over Alaska and crashes, leaving him and his combat dog Odin 58 miles from the nearest road. Over a brutal week he breaks his arm in a river, nearly drowns, and is mauled defending Odin from a wolf pack, popping aspirin to keep his heart going. Near the end of the trek, wrecked by injuries and cardiac failure, he writes a letter for whoever finds Odin, gives the dog a final command to 'find the road', and dies alone in the wild. The film's opening flash-forward pays off as Odin emerges onto the road and is picked up by a young woman named Amber.
notes: Released September 25, 2026. Early recaps agree James dies and Odin lives; sources differ slightly on whether the wolf injuries or his heart is the proximate cause.

title: The Adventures of Cliff Booth
verdict_short: Not released yet.
how: Standalone sequel to Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, written by Quentin Tarantino and directed by David Fincher. Set in 1977 Los Angeles, eight years after the Manson fight, with Cliff now working as a Hollywood studio fixer. No plot or ending has been released. The verdict lands here the week it opens.
notes: Formerly titled The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. Cast includes Elizabeth Debicki, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Scott Caan and Peter Weller.
unreleased: In IMAX Nov 25, 2026. On Netflix Dec 23, 2026.
